verdict: Conditionally support a bounded post-O2 removal slice for explicitly proven private/closed-world, CGU-local, actually use-empty definitions. Existing nonforeign candidate generation is not independently a private ABI proof.
validation: Read-only source review; no build, runtime test, candidate count or performance measurement.

evidence.finding: The original O2 pipeline already contains GlobalDCE; simply adding another run without linkage authority does not solve externally visible unused definitions.
Defined GlobalObjects that are not discardable if unused are marked live. External body definitions survive even when the current module has no uses.
Current complete default<O2> runs before verify and machine emission, with no late internalize/DCE step. Insert the bounded transformation after O2 success and before the existing final LLVM verify.

Explicit closed-executable candidates include all nonforeign source functions and lc1 variants. Cross-unit checks inspect function operand references and global initializer symbols, including imported available_externally bodies. This proves a conservative model reference closure, not independent private ABI status.
Existing closed-executable/anonymous-closure internalization occurs on partitioned model units before O2; it is not the proposed late transform.
LirView has no source visibility/export table. No new private provenance can be inferred from this API alone.
root_functions includes all root nonforeign functions, so it is not a source public/private list.

Internalize preserves declarations, available_externally, dllexport and special roots; it changes visibility/linkage and handles comdat. llvm.used targets are always preserved; compiler.used must remain as a root. Avoid a blanket internalize invocation.

minimum_slice: Keep original CGU partition and complete original O2/inlining pipeline exactly before the new step.

Supply a current, exact producer/verified-project private-or-closed-world authorization for named machine definitions. Unknown provenance declines. Compiler symbol spelling and nonforeign status alone grant nothing.

Require exactly one canonical definition and conservative complete cross-CGU reference closure from current model functions and global initializers; do not discard canonical functions referenced by imported bodies in other CGUs.
At post-O2 boundary select only authorized External definitions with actual use_empty and no address escape, exported ABI, aliases/ifunc/comdat/asm or used/ctor/dtor/annotation reference path.
Internalize only definitions selected for immediate removal, then run GlobalDCE once and retain original LLVM final verification. Do not internalize live definitions or rerun default<O2>.
Include policy and exact candidate/authorization bindings in object/native product identity; preserve independent language Verify, limits and successful-publication rules.
All remaining definitions run the original full machine pipeline. Original inline decisions and live function linkage remain unchanged by this first slice.
nearest_counterexamples: Current module use_empty while another CGU still calls or takes the canonical address.
A symbol exists solely for external ABI, module assembly, llvm.used or a global/alias/ifunc initializer; it has no direct instruction call users.
Treating all nonforeign zil.fn definitions or TypedProgram.root_functions as private lacks the needed visibility/ABI provenance.
Applying early internalization changes O2 inline/deletion decisions and is a different already-measured policy.
quality_and_performance_limits: The source mechanism explains why external unused copies can remain, but does not prove that the reported 424 versus Rust28 definitions are removable. Removing dead definitions changes object layout; no runtime/code-quality/performance outcome is claimed. Actual original425 fresh same-policy oracle and measurements are pending.
